# Glossary {#sec-glossary}

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| A1 / A2 | The two alleles of a SNP in PLINK 1.9 files. Effect sizes (OR, BETA) are always for A1. By default A1 is the minor allele |
| Allele frequency, MAF | Share of chromosome copies carrying an allele; MAF is the frequency of the rarer one |
| Call rate / missing rate | Share of genotypes read successfully; call rate = 1 − missing rate |
| Case / control | Affected (coded 2) / unaffected (coded 1) animal for a yes/no trait |
| CNV | Copy number variant: a deleted or duplicated stretch of DNA |
| Covariate | An extra variable in a model (PCs, sex, herd, age) used to remove its influence |
| D, D′, r² | Measures of linkage disequilibrium between two SNPs (Chapter 9) |
| Dosage | Expected number of copies of an allele (A1 in PLINK 1.9, usually ALT in a VCF) after imputation, between 0 and 2 |
| DR2, R2, INFO | Imputation quality scores: the estimated r² between dosage and true genotype, from BEAGLE, Minimac and IMPUTE respectively |
| Eigenvalue | How much variation lies along a principal component |
| Eigenvector | The direction of a principal component; its values are the PC scores |
| EMP1 / EMP2 | Empirical p-value from permutation / the same, corrected for all tests |
| Epistasis | Interaction between two or more loci |
| F (inbreeding) | Excess homozygosity compared with expectation |
| F_ROH | Share of the genome covered by runs of homozygosity |
| Founder / nonfounder | Animal with both parents unknown / animal with at least one parent in the data |
| F~ST~ | Share of genetic variation that lies between populations |
| GRM | Genomic relationship matrix: relationships between animals estimated from SNPs |
| HWE | Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium: genotype shares p², 2pq and q² under random mating |
| IBS / IBD | Identical by state (same alleles) / identical by descent (same ancestral copy) |
| Imputation | Predicting genotypes that were not measured, using a reference panel |
| KING | A relatedness method that does not need population allele frequencies |
| λ (lambda) | Genomic inflation factor: median test statistic divided by its expected value; close to 1 is good |
| LD pruning | Removing SNPs so that the remaining ones are not strongly correlated |
| LE (linkage equilibrium) | Alleles at two SNPs combined at random on chromosomes; the expected haplotype frequency is the product of the allele frequencies |
| Li and Stephens model | The "copying model" behind most phasing and imputation programs: a chromosome is described as a mosaic of pieces copied from other haplotypes |
| MDS | Multidimensional scaling of pairwise distances; an alternative to PCA |
| Mendel error | A calf genotype that is impossible given its parents' genotypes |
| Mixed model | Regression with a random polygenic effect whose covariance follows the GRM; corrects for relatives and structure together |
| OR / BETA | Odds ratio (yes/no trait) / regression slope (measured trait) per copy of A1 |
| PCA | Principal component analysis: a few axes that summarize genetic differences between animals |
| Phase | Which alleles sit together on the same chromosome copy; `0\|1` in a VCF is phased, `0/1` unphased |
| PI_HAT | Estimated share of the genome two animals share IBD |
| Population stratification | False associations caused by differences in both allele frequency and trait between groups |
| Reference panel | Animals typed at high density (or sequenced) and phased, used to impute others |
| ROH | Run of homozygosity: a long homozygous stretch inherited from a common ancestor |
| Strand flip | The same SNP reported from the opposite DNA strand (A/G becomes T/C) |
| Switch error | A place where an estimated haplotype jumps from one true chromosome copy to the other; the switch error rate measures phasing accuracy |
| TDT | Transmission disequilibrium test: a family-based association test |
| Wahlund effect | Fewer heterozygotes than expected when separate populations are pooled |
